Co-change repulsion: files that change together wire togetherSIMULATEDMEASURED

On hono's history FireTrident redid more work than locks. Part of it: agents took intents whose files are coupled to files other agents were changing, and read-set validation sent them back. TrunkDO now mines the trunk's history at import into a co-change map (Hebbian: a file's weight to a partner estimates P(partner changes | file changes) and decays only as that file changes again; STDP: an author's follow-up commit, or a follow-up intent, potentiates earlier-file → later-file edges). It learns every landing after that. ColonyDO.take adds 2 × coupling × claim for each claimed neighbor of a candidate's files, so a claim repels work on the files that change with it.

Live steering on a preview deployment (MEASURED: real import of hono, real mining, real takes)

Each round a fresh agent claims src/jsx/components.ts (priority 5), then a fresh agent chooses between Y (priority 2.5) and src/utils/body.ts (priority 2). In the coupled colony Y co-changes with the claimed file in hono's last 200 commits; in the control colony it never did.

colonyYtook Ytook Zothertake p50 ms
coupledsrc/jsx/streaming.ts2/2014/204319
controlsrc/router/reg-exp-router/node.ts16/203/201292

Two-sided Fisher exact test on took Y / took Z, coupled vs control: p = 3.0e-5. "Other" rounds are B declining both (the response-threshold rule) or A not taking X first.

  • Rework falls, throughput holds on per-lane landing. At 1,000 agents rework drops from 42.5% to 38.7% at the same 85.9 landings/min; at 100 agents from 12.3% to 10.0% with slightly more landings. Locks stay at 21.7%.
  • With group commit it is a trade. Rework 45.3% → 40.4%, landings 205 → 192/min at 1,000 agents, and draining a fixed backlog slows a little: repelled intents sit in the 200-oldest candidate window until their neighbors land. FT_COCHANGE_WEIGHT tunes it (0 turns it off).
  • What is left of the gap to locks (SIMULATED analysis, not built): direct overlap is only soft repulsion, so the age term and reinforced thresholds let agents take claimed files anyway. Treating a direct overlap as exclusion takes rework to 33.9%, and adding co-change to 31.2% (weight 2) or 26.5% (weight 10), at 86 landings/min, against locks' 21.7% at 52.
  • Method. The simulator's take adds the same core neighborRepulsion ColonyDO uses, with neighbors mined from hono's last 200 first-parent commits (TrunkDO's import depth), top 8 per file, coupling ≥ 0.1. Tasks are drawn from the co-change graph of hono's whole history, while the colony's map knows only the last 200 commits, as a fresh import does. The simulated colony does not learn from its own landings (the deployed TrunkDO does).
